status_reasoning: Reviewers explicitly challenge the interpretation that the muscle arm phenotype represents a defect in 'synapse specificity.' They state 'the data do not address a synaptic function of Notch' and that 'the concept of synapse specificity...is an interpretation that is not directly addressed by the data.' The reviewers request substantial revision to focus on muscle arm formation rather than synaptic specificity claims.

The reviewers do not challenge the core findings about the Notch-Delta pathway components (APX-1, LIN-12, SEL-12) and their cell-autonomous/non-autonomous functions in muscle arm development. They acknowledge the data 'document an interesting muscle differentiation program' controlled by Notch, implicitly accepting these mechanistic findings about the pathway.

The reviewers do not question the findings about UNC-40/DCC and MADD-2 regulation by Notch signaling or their roles in muscle arm formation. These molecular findings about downstream effectors are implicitly accepted as part of the 'developmental program for muscle arm formation controlled by Notch' that reviewers acknowledge.

The reviewers do not challenge the phenotypic characterization of lin-12 and related mutants showing absence of muscle arms, normal vulval morphogenesis, and egg-laying defects. These observations are accepted as documenting 'the muscle arm phenotype' and 'the participation of the muscle cell in synapse development through muscle arm formation.'

Reviewers explicitly request additional analysis, stating 'there was discussion among the reviewers regarding whether the absence of Notch signaling in vm2 partially switches fate or has a more selective disruption of the muscle arm growth program.' They request 'analysis of more fate markers and a more detailed description of morphological features' to clarify this issue, indicating the current evidence is insufficient to resolve this question.

The reviewers do not challenge findings about the independence of pre- and postsynaptic development or that neurons are not required for muscle arm formation. These findings support the reviewers' acknowledgment that the data document 'a muscle differentiation program that precedes postsynaptic differentiation,' which is consistent with these independence claims.

The reviewers do not question the temporal findings about when LIN-12/Notch functions or its independence from earlier developmental roles. These claims about developmental timing are implicitly accepted as part of documenting 'the developmental program for muscle arm formation controlled by Notch.'
